description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.focus: Round 4. Verify the round-3 fixes (commit 2c7c6b5): lint rule value/call-argument/callback coverage, pseudo-catalog field values, theme no-toggle e2e skip semantics, nginx Host guard (421) and /api 404, X-Forwarded-For overwrite and hidden backend headers, tools/container-smoke.mjs, routePath, the docs/qa recordings exemption. Check against the spec delta and design.md. Do NOT re-report what design.md lists under "Accepted limits (review round 3)" or the documented backend-port and DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME follow-ups; report only defects in shipped behaviour or tests that can pass while the spec is violated.

findings.title: docs/qa recordings exemption still covers PDFs, fonts and images named in any key of any manifest
findings.evidence: `recordedFiles` walks every string value in every `docs/qa/**/manifest.json` and exempts it if `MEDIA.test(v)`. MEDIA includes pdf, djvu, epub, fonts and every image type, not just recording formats. So `{"note": "scan.pdf"}` in a hand-written manifest exempts `docs/qa/x/scan.pdf`, which could be a workbook scan (NFR-4). The spec only exempts files a manifest "lists as recordings". The round-3 fix narrowed this from "any string" to "any media string" but did not limit it to recordings.
findings.suggestion: Accept only the recorder's clip/screenshot field (e.g. `clips[].file`), and only recording types (webm/mp4/png). Add a test case where a `.pdf` listed in a manifest is still reported.

findings.title: No-toggle e2e only clicks a select/combobox, so a theme picker built as a select is never switched
findings.evidence: CONTROLS includes `select` and `[role=combobox]`, but the loop only calls `control.click(...)`. Clicking a native `<select>` opens its popup and changes no value, so a Light/Dark/System select passes the check without its options ever being chosen. The spec scenario says every select on a route is "activated". Only the static source regex would catch such a picker.
findings.suggestion: For `select`, call `selectOption` for each option and check the theme after each one. For comboboxes and listboxes, open them and click each `[role=option]` that appears.

findings.title: Static theme guard misses dynamic theme classes and token overrides
findings.evidence: `THEME_WRITE` only matches `classList.x(` when a quote follows right away (`['"`](dark|light|theme)`). It misses `classList.toggle(isDark ? 'dark' : 'light')`, `documentElement.className = 'dark'`, and an app.css rule that redefines `--paper` under `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` or a class. The e2e defers to this test for every screen with no control, which today is all of them, so it is the only FR-58 guard that actually runs.
findings.suggestion: Also match `className\s*=`, `setAttribute('class'` and any `classList.*(...)` containing dark/light/theme. Fail when an app `.css` file redefines a design-system colour token (`--paper`, `--ink`, …).

findings.title: Lint rule exempts the `name` key in nested objects, though `name` is display text on most components
findings.evidence: `NON_TEXT_KEYS = new Set([...NON_TEXT_PROPS, "value", "name"])` skips the `name` key in every object literal. As a prop, `name` is treated as text except on Icon and ChoiceGroup, and `SubjectTile` shows `name` (game.tsx:54). So `<SubjectList items={[{ name: 'Matematika' }]} />` passes lint, while `<SubjectTile name="Matematika" />` is reported. The two cases contradict each other.
findings.suggestion: Remove `name` from NON_TEXT_KEYS, or exempt it only where `value`/`id` sits beside it (ChoiceOption-style objects). Add an invalid case for `{ name: 'Matematika' }` inside a component prop.

findings.title: Call-argument coverage flags locale and format arguments, so idiomatic Intl formatting fails lint
findings.evidence: Every literal argument of any call is now reported (`...node.arguments.flatMap(literalTexts)`). Only `t()` is exempt. So `{n.toLocaleString('cs-CZ')}`, `{d.toLocaleDateString('cs', { month: 'long' })}` and `<Stat value={x.toFixed(1)} unit=... />`-style formatting all fail with `error`. Locale tags and Intl options are not UI text. This pushes later slices (admin stats) toward eslint-disable comments, which turn the rule off for real literals too.
findings.suggestion: Skip arguments of known formatting methods (`toLocaleString`, `toLocaleDateString`, `toLocaleTimeString`, `Intl.*` constructors), or skip BCP-47-shaped strings and the values of Intl option objects. Add valid test cases for both.

findings.title: Container smoke PASS is claimed with no evidence file, and the Host guard has no static test
findings.evidence: tasks.md says "`npm run test:container` … (all PASS 2026-10-04)". But `tools/container-smoke.mjs` only prints to the console and writes no report under docs/qa. `test:container` is also not run by qa:verify. container-config.test.ts checks XFF and the hidden headers, but has no assertion for the `default_server` `return 421`, the `server_name` allow-list or `location = /api { return 404; }`. A regression in the DNS-rebinding guard would pass the whole battery. AGENTS.md requires done-claims to carry a resolvable evidence pointer.
findings.suggestion: Have container-smoke write its PASS/FAIL lines to `docs/qa/container-smoke-latest.md` and cite that file in tasks.md. Add static assertions to container-config.test.ts for the 421 default server, the server_name pattern and the `/api` 404 location.

findings.title: nginx passes client-supplied Forwarded / X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Port headers to the backend
findings.evidence: The round-3 fix overwrites X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto. The `location /api/` block still passes every other client header to the backend unchanged. That includes RFC 7239 `Forwarded: for=6.6.6.6`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-Port`. With Spring's `server.forward-headers-strategy=framework` (ForwardedHeaderFilter), `Forwarded` takes precedence over X-Forwarded-For. A LAN attacker could then send a new `Forwarded: for=<random>` on each admin login attempt and get past the per-IP login throttle that this fix was meant to protect. That allows unlimited password guessing against the bcrypt admin account. A spoofed X-Forwarded-Host/Port also flows into Tomcat RemoteIpValve and Spring absolute-URL and redirect building. I could not read ../backend (permission denied), so I could not confirm which forward-headers strategy it uses. That is why confidence is medium. `tools/container-smoke.mjs` sends only a spoofed X-Forwarded-For, so it passes while this path is open.
findings.suggestion: Make nginx the only source of forwarding headers. In `location /api/`, add `proxy_set_header Forwarded "";`, `proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;`, `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host "";` (or `$host`) and `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port "";` (or `$server_port`). In container-smoke.mjs, also send `Forwarded: for=6.6.6.6` and `X-Real-IP: 6.6.6.6`, and assert that the stub's echo contains neither. Extend the spec scenario 'Spoofed client address' to cover all of these headers.

findings.title: docs/qa recordings exemption also covers PDFs, photos and fonts listed in any docs/qa manifest.json
findings.evidence: `recordedFiles` exempts any string in any `docs/qa/**/manifest.json` that matches MEDIA. MEDIA includes pdf, jpg, heic, psd, woff2 and djvu, not only the clip and screenshot formats the recorder writes. A contributor or agent could commit a workbook scan (`docs/qa/demo/page.pdf` or `scan.jpg`) together with a hand-written `docs/qa/demo/manifest.json` that names it. The NFR-4 provenance test would then report nothing, and workbook content would enter git unchecked. Nothing requires the manifest to come from scripts/record-demos.mjs.
findings.suggestion: Limit the exemption to the formats the recorder actually produces, for example `/\.(webm|mp4|png|gif)$/i`. Also require the manifest entry to have the recorder's shape (for example `clips[].file` with `frs`), not any string anywhere in the JSON. Add a negative test with `docs/qa/demo/page.pdf` listed in a manifest.

findings.title: The theme no-toggle checks miss a native <select> theme picker and className-based theme switches
findings.evidence: The spec says every select on a route is activated. The e2e only calls `click()` on `select`. That opens the native dropdown but never changes the value, so `onChange` never runs. A 'Light/Dark' `<select>` that writes a theme class would pass the e2e. The static backstop (src/app/theme-source.test.ts:12, THEME_WRITE) catches `data-theme`, `dataset.theme`, `colorScheme` and `classList.x('dark'|'light'|'theme…')`. It does not catch `document.documentElement.className = 'dark'`, `setAttribute('class', 'theme-dark')` or `classList.toggle(isDark ? 'dark' : 'light')`. So both layers can pass while the FR-58 'no in-app toggle' requirement is broken.
findings.suggestion: In the e2e, handle `select` (and `[role=combobox]` listboxes) by calling `selectOption` for each option, then re-check `[data-theme]` and the body `--paper`. Extend THEME_WRITE to also match `className\s*=` and `setAttribute\(\s*['"]class` when combined with dark/light/theme, and conditional `classList` arguments that contain those words.

findings.title: The provenance exemption covers PDFs, e-books and fonts listed in a docs/qa manifest, not just recordings
findings.evidence:
Coverage summary: 18 scenarios: 15 implemented, 3 partial, 0 missing, 0 contradicted.

Spec (Unlisted asset fails): the only exemptions are `contract/` and "the media files a `docs/qa/**/manifest.json` lists as recordings". The spec counts PDFs as documents, not media ("a media, document or data file"). Code: `recordedFiles` exempts any string that matches `MEDIA`, and `MEDIA` (line 17-18) includes `pdf|djvu|epub|woff2?|ttf|otf|psd|ai|eps|svg`. So a manifest under docs/qa that lists `"workbook.pdf"` makes `docs/qa/<dir>/workbook.pdf` exempt from the manifest check. That is exactly the workbook content NFR-4 forbids, and the provenance test still passes.
findings.suggestion: Limit the recording exemption to what scripts/record-demos.mjs writes: a RECORDINGS regex such as /\.(webm|mp4|png|jpe?g|gif)$/i, or better, only the manifest's clip/file fields. Add a unit case where a manifest lists `scan.pdf` and the file is still reported.

findings.title: The 421 response from the Host guard has no security headers
findings.evidence: Spec (Served behind one origin): "Every response SHALL carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and a Content-Security-Policy with … `frame-ancestors 'none'`". The `default_server` block (lines 7-11) has only `server_tokens off; return 421;`. The three `add_header … always` directives sit in the second server block, so the 421 page (nginx's default HTML error body) is sent without nosniff, a Referrer-Policy or a CSP. container-smoke.mjs:115 checks only the status, so the gap is never caught.
findings.suggestion: Add the same three `add_header … always` lines to the default_server block, or move them into a shared include. Extend container-smoke so the 421 response is checked for all three headers.

findings.title: The Host guard (421) has no check in the qa:verify battery
findings.evidence: Spec scenario (Foreign host name): "/api/health with Host: evil.example → 421 and the backend is not reached". container-config.test.ts asserts X-Forwarded-For, proxy_hide_header and X-Forwarded-Proto (lines 50-59) but nothing about `default_server`, `return 421` or the `server_name` allow-list. A grep for 421, default_server and server_name in that file finds nothing. The only check is tools/container-smoke.mjs:115, run by `npm run test:container`. That script is not referenced from package.json's battery, scripts/ or trace/acceptance-contracts.json, and with `--e2e` it exits 1 until the documented DOUCKO_CHILD_DISPLAY_NAME follow-up lands. Deleting the guard or widening `server_name` to `_` would leave `npm run qa:verify` green.
findings.suggestion: Add static assertions to container-config.test.ts: a `listen 80 default_server` block that returns 421, a server_name limited to localhost and the IPv4 regex, and no `_`/catch-all name in the serving block. Alternatively, wire the container smoke's HTTP checks (without --e2e) into an acceptance contract.

findings.title: Client-supplied Forwarded and X-Forwarded-Host/Port headers still reach the backend
findings.evidence: The spec requires forwarding "the connecting client address (never a client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For`)" so the per-IP login throttle cannot be spoofed. nginx overwrites X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto but passes a client's `Forwarded: for=6.6.6.6`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-Port` through unchanged. If the backend honours RFC 7239 `Forwarded` (Spring's ForwardedHeaderFilter / forward-headers-strategy=framework prefers it over X-Forwarded-For), the spoof the scenario forbids comes back through another header. I could not verify the backend's setting (no read access to ../backend/src/main).
findings.suggestion: Add `proxy_set_header Forwarded "";`, `proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;`, `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;` and `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port $server_port;`, plus a container-smoke check that a client `Forwarded: for=6.6.6.6` does not reach the stub.

findings.title: The lint rule exempts every argument of t(), so literal interpolation values pass
findings.evidence: Spec: the rule SHALL refuse literal UI text in "call arguments" (tasks 2.2: "accepts catalog calls"). Code: `if (node.callee.type === "Identifier" && CATALOG_LOOKUPS.has(node.callee.name)) return [];` returns before any argument is inspected. So `{t('greeting', { name: 'Ahoj' })}` or `{t('x', { unit: 'bodů' })}` renders literal Czech text with no lint error. Only the first argument is a key; the params object is shown text. A related gap: an immediately invoked callee, `{(() => 'Ahoj')()}`, is not inspected either, because only a MemberExpression callee's receiver is checked.
findings.suggestion:
Exempt only `node.arguments[0]` of t() and run literalTexts over the remaining arguments (honouring NON_TEXT_KEYS such as `count`). Also inspect function-expression callees. Add an invalid case `

{t('x', { name: 'Ahoj' })}

` to lint-rule.test.ts.

result.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism; it is in the code as described. `recordedFiles` (src/test/provenance.test.ts:78-92) walks every value of every `docs/qa/**/manifest.json`, whatever key it sits under. At line 84 the only filter is `MEDIA.test(v)`. MEDIA (line 17-18) includes pdf, djvu, epub, fonts, psd/ai/eps and every image type, not just recording formats. Any string that ends in `.pdf` is therefore resolved against the manifest's folder and added to `listed`. `inScope` (line 32) then drops that path, so a workbook scan at `docs/qa/x/scan.pdf` would never be reported if a manifest has e.g. `{"note":"scan.pdf"}`.

Nothing else guards against this:
- The manifest.json files are not checked themselves. They are not MEDIA or DOCUMENTS, and SOURCE_DATA only covers src/ and e2e/. A hand-written or edited manifest is never validated.
- The test at line 137 passes only because the note is `'scan.pdf is fine'`, which does not end in `.pdf`, so the regex fails. It does not cover a bare `"scan.pdf"`.
- The module doc (line 12) says only "recordings a manifest lists are exempt", so exempting any media string under any key is broader than intended.

The bug is real, but triggering it takes a manifest.json under docs/qa that names a non-recording file in some field. That is an unusual misuse or a deliberate bypass, not a normal workflow, so I'd downgrade the severity from major to minor/moderate.

The mechanism is real. In src/test/provenance.test.ts:78-92, `recordedFiles` walks every string value at any depth of every `docs/qa/**/manifest.json`. The only filter is `MEDIA.test(v)` (line 84), and MEDIA (line 18) includes pdf, djvu, epub, fonts and all image types, not just recording formats. So a manifest containing `{"note":"scan.pdf"}` at docs/qa/x/manifest.json puts `docs/qa/x/scan.pdf` into the exemption set. `inScope` (line 32) then drops it, and an unlisted workbook PDF passes the NFR-4 check. The existing test (line 137) only shows that `'scan.pdf is fine'` is rejected, and that is only because the string doesn't end in `.pdf`. A bare `'scan.pdf'` in `note` would be accepted. The real recorder (scripts/record-demos.mjs:19,105) writes `{kind, results:[{id, proof, video, screenshot, explainer, asserted}]}`, so the check could be limited to `results[].video` / `results[].screenshot` with webm/mp4/png types, as the finding suggests. The spec comment (line 12) says only "recordings a manifest lists" are exempt, so this does diverge from the stated contract.

Exploitability: this is a hole in a CI guard, not a runtime bug a user can hit. To trigger it, someone has to commit a PDF under docs/qa/ and also add a manifest.json beside it that names the PDF. A normal recorder run never does this, because it only writes clip and screenshot paths. So it can't happen by accident in the normal flow. It needs a hand-written or edited manifest, for example an agent trying to get a failing provenance check to pass. That can happen, but it's a deliberate step, which is why I'd downgrade from major to minor. The mechanism itself is confirmed and easy to reproduce with a single JSON key.

The finding holds. `e2e/theme.spec.ts:9-12` lists `select` and `[role=combobox]` in CONTROLS, but the loop at lines 30-40 only calls `control.click()` before checking the theme. In Playwright, clicking a native `<select>` focuses it and may open its popup, but it never changes the selected value. A Light/Dark/System `<select>` (the default is usually System or OS) would therefore pass with no option ever chosen. A custom combobox is the same: one click opens the listbox, and the `[role=option]` items that appear afterwards are not picked up, because `count()` is re-read each loop and `nth(i)` indices shift. The test therefore doesn't really cover selects. The spec scenario (`openspec/changes/implement-platform-foundation-ui/specs/platform-foundation/spec.md:25`) says every "select on a route is activated", which this code doesn't do for selects. Nothing else in the e2e covers it. The comment in `src/app/theme-source.test.ts` says the e2e "activates every control", so the static test doesn't make up for the gap. It is only a regex backstop, as the finding says. The severity stays minor: there is probably no theme select today, so this is a hole in a guard test, not a defect users would see.

The mechanism holds. At e2e/theme.spec.ts:33 the loop only calls `control.click()` on every match of CONTROLS, and CONTROLS includes `select` and `[role=combobox]`. In Playwright, clicking a native `<select>` does not choose an option, and clicking a combobox only opens it, so a Light/Dark select would pass the check without being switched. As an e2e check it really is incomplete.

It is only a latent test gap, though, not something a user or attacker can hit today:
1. No app source under src/ has a `<select>` or a combobox, so no theme picker exists for this check to miss.
2. src/app/theme-source.test.ts statically rejects any app source that contains `data-theme`, `dataset.theme`, `colorScheme`, `color-scheme`, or a `classList.*('dark'|'light'|'theme'…)` call. A select-based picker would almost certainly use one of these to write the theme, so this unit test would fail on it. The finding admits this backstop exists.

A regression would need both a new select picker and a way of applying the theme that the regex does not match (for example, setting inline style variables directly). That makes this a hardening suggestion.

Verdict: the claim is technically correct, so it is not refuted. Downgrade it to nit/low.

Partly right. `THEME_WRITE` (src/app/theme-source.test.ts:12) is `/data-theme|dataset\.theme|colorScheme|color-scheme|classList\.\w+\(\s*['"`](dark|light|theme)/`, and some of the finding's examples are overstated:
- **`@media (prefers-color-scheme)` is caught.** The literal `color-scheme` matches it, so that example is wrong.
- **A `dark` or `light` class does nothing on its own.** `classList.toggle(isDark ? 'dark' : 'light')` and `className = 'dark'` are missed by the regex. But the design system switches themes only through `[data-theme=...]` and the `prefers-color-scheme` media query (tokens.css:3, 50, 83-84). It has no `.dark` or `.light` selectors, so those writes would not change the theme.

The real gap is the one the finding names last. An app `.css` rule that redefines a design-system colour token under a class, such as `.night { --paper: …; --ink: … }`, matches none of the alternatives. A JS call like `document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--paper', …)` also slips through. Pair either with any class toggle and a control can switch the theme while this test stays green, which breaks FR-58.

This test is the only guard for screens with no controls: e2e/theme.spec.ts:43 skips those and points to it. So the token-override hole matters. The suggested fix (fail when app CSS or JS redefines a design-system colour token) is the meaningful part. Widening the class-name matching would add little.

The mechanism is confirmed for token overrides but overstated for class names and media queries, so the severity stays minor.

The regex reading is accurate: `classList\.\w+\(\s*['"`](dark|light|theme)` only matches a quoted literal right after the paren. But the evasions the finding lists would not switch the theme in this codebase. `src/design-system/tokens.css` picks the theme in only two ways: `[data-theme="light"|"dark"]` (lines 3 and 50) and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-theme="light"])` (lines 83–84). It has no `.dark`, `.light` or `.theme-*` selector. So `classList.toggle(isDark ? 'dark' : 'light')` or `documentElement.className = 'dark'` would do nothing to colours, and there is nothing for the guard to catch. Any route that does work goes through `data-theme`, and the regex matches that string anywhere, including `setAttribute('data-theme', …)` and `dataset.theme`. An app.css rule that redefines `--paper` under `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` still follows the OS, so it is not an FR-58 violation either.

The one theoretical gap needs two new pieces of code: an app CSS class that redefines several design-system tokens, plus a control that toggles that class. Nothing like that exists today. A grep of `src/` outside the design system finds no `classList`, no `className =` assignment and no `--paper`/`--ink` definitions. The only `className` uses are static JSX strings in `App.tsx`, `Shell.tsx` and `NotFound.tsx`. AGENTS.md also forbids raw hex in app styles (tokens only), and code review would reject it. Neither a user nor an attacker can trigger this now. It is a speculative hardening idea for a test, not a correctness defect.
